sub_graphs.title: EIP-684: Contract Address Collision Detection
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation logic that detects and prevents contract deployment at addresses with existing state

nodes.label: Contract Creation Initiated
nodes.description: A CREATE, CREATE2, or creation transaction has been initiated

nodes.label: Compute Target Address
nodes.description: Calculate the destination address for the new contract based on sender and nonce (CREATE) or salt (CREATE2)

nodes.label: Target Address Computed
nodes.description: The address where the contract would be deployed has been determined

nodes.label: Check Address Nonce
nodes.description: Read the nonce of the target address from world state

nodes.label: Check Address Code Length
nodes.description: Read the code length of the target address from world state

nodes.label: Nonce is Non-Zero
nodes.description: Target address has nonce > 0, indicating previous transactions

nodes.label: Code Length is Non-Zero
nodes.description: Target address has existing contract code deployed

nodes.label: Address is Empty
nodes.description: Target address has nonce == 0 AND code length == 0

nodes.label: Collision Detected
nodes.description: Address collision found - deployment must fail

nodes.label: No Collision
nodes.description: Address is available for deployment

external_entities.name: Contract Deployer
external_entities.description: EOA or contract initiating contract creation via transaction or CREATE/CREATE2

sub_graphs.title: EIP-684: Collision Exception Behavior
sub_graphs.description: Models how the EVM handles contract creation when a collision is detected

nodes.label: Collision Confirmed
nodes.description: Collision detection has confirmed address is not empty

nodes.label: Treat as Invalid Opcode
nodes.description: Handle collision as if first byte of init code was invalid opcode

nodes.label: Consume Remaining Gas
nodes.description: Consume all gas allocated to the creation operation

nodes.label: Revert State Changes
nodes.description: Roll back any state modifications from this call frame

nodes.label: Creation Failed
nodes.description: Contract creation has failed atomically

nodes.label: Return Zero Address
nodes.description: Push zero address to stack (for CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes)

nodes.label: Caller Notified of Failure
nodes.description: Calling context receives indication of creation failure

sub_graphs.title: EIP-684: Code Immutability Enforcement
sub_graphs.description: Models how EIP-684 enforces the security property of deployed code immutability

nodes.label: Contract Deployed at Address
nodes.description: A contract with code exists at a given address

nodes.label: Attacker Computes Collision Address
nodes.description: Attacker has computed an address matching an existing contract

nodes.label: Attempt Malicious Deployment
nodes.description: Attacker attempts to deploy different code at the collision address

nodes.label: Collision Check Executes
nodes.description: EIP-684 collision detection runs before init code execution

nodes.label: Attack Blocked
nodes.description: Collision detection has prevented the malicious deployment

nodes.label: Original Code Preserved
nodes.description: The original contract code remains unchanged and immutable

external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
external_entities.description: Attacker attempting to replace existing contract code via address collision

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions 'nonzero nonce' but does not clarify if this includes the nonce increment that happens as part of the creation process
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the check happens against the pre-creation state. The nonce at the target address before any modifications from this transaction must be zero.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly address the case of addresses with balance but zero nonce and zero code
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume balance alone does not trigger collision. Only nonce > 0 OR code.length > 0 causes collision detection to fail the creation.

implicit_assumptions.description: Computing an address collision with an existing contract requires computational resources comparable to a preimage attack on Keccak-256
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If collision computation becomes feasible, attackers could prepare CREATE2 deployments that later collide with valuable contracts

implicit_assumptions.description: The world state accurately reflects all deployed contracts and their addresses
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: State corruption could allow collision check bypass, enabling code replacement attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: The CREATE2 salt and init code hash provide sufficient uniqueness to prevent accidental collisions between different deployers
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Factory contracts could accidentally create collisions if they reuse salts with different init codes

implicit_assumptions.description: All Ethereum clients implement the collision check identically and atomically
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Consensus failures could occur if clients disagree on collision detection results
